newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian rouble dives as funds come from T-bill mkt.
newsitem.headline: Russian rouble dives as funds come from T-bill mkt.

text.p: The Russian rouble fell sharply on Thursday after several days of strength as free funds came into the market from the T-bill market, dealers said.
T-bills and bonds edged up slightly in lethargic trading.
*Average yield fell to 18.2 pct from 18.4 pct on Wednesday
*Turnover rose to 3.93 trln rbls from 2.27 trln rbls
*Central bank sold 238 bln rbls of bills
The rouble was under strong upwards pressure last week as banks bought the national currency ahead of an auction of 25 plus one share in national telecoms holding Svyazinvest.
Bidders for the auction, the results of which will be announced on Friday, had to deposit either $400 million or a little over two trillion roubles by July 21.
The shortage of roubles was reinforced on Wednesday when banks bid a total of 14.6 trillion roubles for government paper at the weekly auctions, and overnight credit rates rose as high as 80 percent.

"The dollar has been looking up for several days already," a Mezhkombank dealer said. "During yesterday's fall the dollar did not reach the central bank's lowest rates. Everyone understood that as soon as overnight credits ease, the dollar will go up."

Many of the rouble funds left in the T-bill market on Thursday were not used to buy bills, as reflected by the modest rise in prices and relatively low turnover, but flowed back into the currency market, dealers said.
Traders said the government securities market was quiet as the current average yield of just under 19 percent was a strong resistance level and there were no new funds able to break it.

Bank Imperial dealer Sergei Gubanov forecast the T-bill market would fluctuate on Friday. He said a slight fall in prices was possible as new funds would come from the natural gas monopoly Gazprom tax payments next week.
